entitySuffixRule: Must contain the words "limited liability company" or "limited company," or the abbreviation "L.L.C.," "LLC," "L.C.," or "LC." "Limited" may be abbreviated as "Ltd." and "company" as "Co." The name may not contain "association," "corporation," "incorporated," "partnership," "limited partnership," or "L.P." Subsection (1) opens with two chapter exceptions: a professional services company under Section 48-3a-1104, and a low-profit limited liability company under Section 48-3a-1302, which must instead carry "L3C" or "l3c" in its name.
distinguishabilityNote: Must be distinguishable, on the records of the Division of Corporations and Commercial Code, from the actual name, reserved name, or assumed/fictitious name of any entity registered with the Division, and from any tradename, trademark, or service mark registered with the Division. The statutory test is that a distinguishable name contains one or more different words, letters, or numerals. Entity-type words and abbreviations, the words "the," "and," "a" and "plus," punctuation and special characters, and capitalization are all disregarded; a difference in singular versus plural form is disregarded only for a company formed in Utah, or registered here as a foreign company, on or after May 4, 1998. Two exceptions, both in subsection (3)(b): the holder of the conflicting name consents in writing and submits an undertaking satisfactory to the Division to change its own name, or the applicant delivers a certified copy of a final judgment of a court of competent jurisdiction establishing its right to the name.
nameReservationCostBasis: The $22 Division of Corporations fee is the full cost of a name reservation.
notes: Restricted words need written consent before the Division will register the name: bank and related terms (Bank, Banker, Banking, Banc, Banque, Banco, Bancorp, Bancorporation, Bankcard, Bancard, Savings Association, Building Association, Savings and Loan Assoc.) require the Department of Financial Institutions; "university," "college," and "institute" require the Division of Consumer Protection under § 53B-5-114; and "Olympic," "Olympiad" and "Citius Altius Fortius" require the written consent of the United States Olympic Committee. Separately, § 48-3a-108 bars the number sequence "911" outright for any LLC formed or renamed on or after May 4, 2022, and bars "association," "corporation," "incorporated," "partnership," "limited partnership" and "L.P." from an LLC name. Two further statutory bars sit outside the distinguishability test: subsection (6) forbids a name implying the company is an agency of the state or a political subdivision when it is not, and subsection (9)(a) forbids anyone other than a Utah LLC or a foreign LLC authorized here from using "limited liability company," "limited company," "L.L.C.," "L.C.," "LLC" or "LC" in a name. "Business trust" must appear as the last words of the name. A name reservation lasts 120 days and can be transferred by signed notice. Note: Utah reorganized its unincorporated-entity code effective 2026-10-01 (Chapter 93, 2026 General Session renumbers Title 48, Chapter 3a to Title 16, Chapter 20), so re-verify the section numbers after that date; the requirements above are current as of 2026-07-25.
